Contributing to bourse

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for your interest in bourse, the grounded market-data connector of the ORCHESTRA analytics framework. This document describes how to propose a change.

The grounding discipline (read this first)

bourse exists to enforce one principle: the Independent Oracle Principle (IOP). Every fact about an exchange – a symbol, a price tick size, a fee, a column’s unit – is [unverified] until it has been diffed against the exchange’s own catalogue or a recorded-real response. A contribution that asserts a new external fact (a new endpoint’s columns, a new symbol’s filters, a new exchange’s conventions) must:

  1. Add the fact to the provenance registry (R/external_facts.R) with the default verified_on = NA.
  2. Ground it against the authority with a recorded-real cassette – a payload captured from the live API by data-raw/record_fixtures.R, never a hand-authored literal. A hand-authored fixture is the circular mock that hides drift; this is a hard rule.
  3. Pin the cassette’s sha256 + md5 in tests/testthat/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md and assert the md5 in a test (the meta-oracle), plus a property / structural oracle on the captured payload.

If a fact cannot be grounded, leave it [unverified] and have the verb refuse, rather than returning a number the package cannot stand behind. Abstention beats a silently wrong number.

Development workflow

  • Iterate with devtools::load_all(); never R CMD INSTALL while the package is loaded.
  • devtools::document() after any roxygen change; devtools::test() before a push; R CMD check --as-cran before a release.
  • Vignettes are .Rmd (the R CMD check --as-cran first-class engine).
  • The package targets a zero-warning --as-cran check.

Code style

Base R plus data.table; snake_case; <- for assignment; TRUE / FALSE spelled out; two-space indentation; lines within roughly 80 characters; pkg::fun() qualification for non-base namespaces; seq_len() / vapply() over unguarded 1:n / sapply(). No tidyverse idioms.

Reporting a bug

Open an issue describing the call, the observed output (including any bourse_refusal), and the expected output. If it concerns a grounding mismatch against the live exchange, include the date and the relevant /exchangeInfo (or endpoint) excerpt – that is exactly the kind of drift bourse is built to catch.

Conduct

By participating you agree to abide by the project’s Code of Conduct (CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
